items.finding: Reframed calcium teaching to avoid overstating fracture prevention from supplementation alone. NIH ODS confirms calcium is required for bone structure and that inadequate calcium contributes to osteoporosis, while evidence for supplementation and fracture reduction in older adults is mixed.
items.source_locator: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, Calcium Fact Sheet for Health Professionals, Bone health in older adults / Calcium deficiency; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Updated to the current CDC recommendation that all women capable of becoming pregnant obtain 400 mcg folic acid daily because neural tube defects occur very early, often before pregnancy is recognized.
items.source_locator: CDC Folic Acid: Sources and Recommended Intake, general recommendation; updated 2026-06-02, reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Retained the 60-minutes-per-day recommendation and specified ages 6-17 plus moderate-to-vigorous intensity. CDC current guidance also specifies vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activity on at least 3 days weekly.
items.source_locator: CDC Child Activity: An Overview, Children and adolescents 6 to 17; updated 2025-12-04, reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: The active-listening concept is clinically reasonable, but the current generic NCBI nursing-fundamentals locator is secondary and too broad for this bank's strict provenance rule. Hold until replaced with a precise professional standard or directly sourced communication guidance.

The culturally responsive care principle is appropriate, but the current broad psychiatry.org citation does not identify an exact guideline section. Hold pending a precise APA/ANA or federal cultural-competence standard locator.

The cumulative-loss risk claim is plausible but the existing generic NCBI source is secondary and does not support a strict single-best-answer item at the required provenance level. Hold pending an authoritative grief/geriatric source with exact locator.

Retained peripheral edema as a recognized adverse effect of dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers but removed wording that could make edema automatically benign or exclude heart-failure assessment. Final item should distinguish class-related edema from clinical evaluation of new edema.
items.source_locator: FDA prescribing information for amlodipine/dihydropyridine CCB adverse reactions; exact product-label revision to be pinned during final integration

items.finding: Reframed statin-associated muscle symptoms so mild aches are not equated with rhabdomyolysis, while still requiring clinical review. Generic FDA label URL is insufficient and must be replaced by an exact statin label and warning section before final pass.

items.finding: Retained hypokalemia and hyponatremia as recognized thiazide risks and removed any implication that hyperkalemia is the principal expected imbalance. Exact hydrochlorothiazide/chlorthalidone label section must replace the generic FDA label URL before final pass.

items.finding: Kept antidepressant discontinuation symptoms after abrupt SSRI cessation but removed colloquial wording as a required diagnostic feature. Final item should use label-supported symptoms and emphasize provider-guided tapering rather than implying one universal taper schedule.
items.source_locator: FDA SSRI prescribing information, Discontinuation Syndrome/Discontinuation Adverse Reactions; exact product label required

items.finding: Retained the clinically important NSAID-lithium interaction: NSAIDs may decrease lithium clearance and increase lithium concentrations/toxicity risk. Exact lithium product label and drug-interaction section must be pinned before final pass.

items.finding: Kept increased bleeding risk with warfarin plus NSAIDs, but revised the explanation so it does not imply that INR must necessarily rise. The principal concern is additive bleeding risk, including GI bleeding, through pharmacodynamic effects and mucosal injury.
items.source_locator: FDA Structured Product Label for warfarin, Drug Interactions/Drugs That Increase Bleeding Risk; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Retained caution with a beta-blocker plus verapamil because both can depress AV conduction and heart rate. The item should avoid implying the combination is universally contraindicated; exact verapamil/beta-blocker label interaction language is required before final pass.

items.finding: Retained buprenorphine as a partial opioid agonist with weaker respiratory-depressant effects than full agonists, but removed any absolute implication that the ceiling effect eliminates overdose risk. SAMHSA explicitly warns that overdose and respiratory distress remain possible, especially with other CNS depressants.
items.source_locator: SAMHSA What is Buprenorphine?, How Does Buprenorphine Work? and Safety Precautions; current page reviewed 2026-08-14
